newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares continue rise in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares continue rise in moderate trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices continued to rise on Sunday in average trade headed by the popular Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, the Capital Market Authority (CMA) said in a report.
The CMA's all-share index closed up 3.1 points at 418.28, its 19th highest level in as many trading days on turnover of 56.64 million pounds ($16.66 million).
"The market is still climbing, there is still demand on stocks but there is no special sector," broker Mohamed Magdi of Hermes/EFG told Reuters.
Medinet Nasr was the day's most actively traded stock with shares worth more than 6.75 million pounds changing hands. It closed 19 pounds higher at 474.

It was followed by North Cairo Flour Mills which closed 7.75 pounds higher at 198 after trading in more than 4.40 million pounds. East Delta Mills traded in more than 1.70 million pounds but shed 1.56 pounds to close at 93.10. Upper Egypt Mills traded in more than 1.35 million pounds but closed 0.75 lower at 107.25, the CMA report said.
The cement sector traded well too, with Amriyah Cement the best of the bunch trading in more than 4.00 million pounds but it closed 3.00 pounds lower at 90.
Suez Cement traded in more than 3.90 million pounds but lost 4.2 pounds to close at 79.8.
Helwan Portland Cement traded in more than 1.40 million pounds but was unchanged at 80.25.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 707.55 points from 700.83 points on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 272.97 points from 271.35 points.
Out of the 79 shares traded, 41 gained, 19 lost and 19 ended the day unchanged.
